facts.fact: WordPerfect Graphic may combine vector drawing and bitmap data.
WPG versions and import restrictions affect legacy WordPerfect graphics.
JPEG is lossy raster encoding without an alpha channel.

methods.steps: Select a range or chart; Home > arrow beside Copy > Copy as Picture > OK. Paste the picture; right-click it, Save as Picture, choose PNG in the Save as type list.

methods.steps: Open the XLS in Calc. File > Export As > Export as PDF. Run mutool draw -o sheet-view-%d.png -r 150 workbook.pdf.
methods.limits: The PDF is an intermediate step.

facts.fact: Excel 97–2003 XLS uses BIFF8; earlier XLS variants also exist.
PNG compresses raster images without a lossy encoding stage.

methods.steps: Python: import pymupdf; doc=pymupdf.open("printed.xps"); doc[0].get_pixmap(dpi=150, alpha=False).save("printed-first.jpeg", jpg_quality=90)
methods.limits: Renders only the first page in this example; loop over pages for a whole document. Writing JPEG needs PyMuPDF 1.22.0 or newer, and the dpi argument of get_pixmap came in 1.19.2.

methods.steps: mutool draw -r 150 -o xps-view-%d.png printed.xps; then magick xps-view-1.png -quality 90 printed-page.jpeg
methods.limits: PNG is an explicit rendered intermediate; repeat the JPEG encoding for each required page.

facts.fact: XPS uses fixed pages and packaging for electronic documents and printing.
MuPDF supports XPS page rendering, but mutool draw does not directly list JPEG among its output image formats.
Ordinary JPEG carries opaque pixels and uses lossy compression.
